history.dynasty: Founded early 18th century; present structure built 1985–1987 (efforts of Kishore Kunal)
history.period: 1730 (founding by Swami Balanand of the Ramanandi sect); 1985–1987 (current structure)
history.summary: One of the most visited Hindu temples in Bihar, the Mahavir Mandir at Mahavir Chowk next to Patna Junction is dedicated to Hanuman and is popularly known as the Manokamna (wish-fulfilling) temple — devotees believe every sincere wish made here is fulfilled. It was established around 1730 by Swami Balanand of the Ramanandi sect and was declared a public temple after a 1948 Patna High Court judgement. The present two-storey Nagara-style marble structure (approx. 10,000 sq ft) dates to 1985–1987; its sanctum holds two Hanuman idols — one for the protection of the good, one for the destruction of the wicked — alongside Rama, Krishna, Durga, Shiva, Ganesha, Buddha and other deities, plus a floating 'Ram Setu' stone. The temple is famous for its Naivedyam ladoo and, through the Sri Mahavir Sthan Nyas Samiti, runs several charitable hospitals in Bihar.

name: Mahavir Mandir
town_description: Patna is the capital of Bihar, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world — ancient Pataliputra, seat of the Mauryan and Gupta empires. It stands on the southern bank of the Ganga and blends ancient heritage (Kumhrar, Agam Kuan) with modern institutions. The city is a major pilgrimage hub with Patna Sahib (Sikh), Patan Devi and Mahavir Mandir drawing devotees year-round.
